https://www.mediafax.ro/english/the-mini.text: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs recalls three romanian consuls general The decision was made Thursday during a cabinet meeting at the proposal of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and was approved by Acting Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan. “Thus, at the government meeting on Thursday, July 23, 2026, the recall of Romania’s consul general in São Paulo (Federative Republic of Brazil), the consul general in Nantes (French Republic), and the consul general in Frankfurt am Main (Federal Republic of Germany) was approved. The consuls general were appointed in the summer of 2024 with the primary task of opening new Romanian consulates general. “During the process of evaluating, identifying, and setting up the consular offices in São Paulo, Nantes, and Frankfurt am Main, the consular offices were not made operational in 2024, in 2025, nor by the new deadlines agreed upon following successive extensions,” the Ministry of Foreign Affairs stated in a press release. The deadline for returning to the country is up to 90 days. https://www.politico.eu/article/kemi-bad.text: LONDON — Kemi Badenoch’s Conservative Party used to discuss who would replace her. Now they want her secret sauce. Almost two years after taking the helm of the Tory party in the wake of its 2024 general election battering, Badenoch’s personal ratings are soaring. YouGov polling, conducted last month , found 38 percent of Brits think Badenoch is doing well as Conservative Party leader — up 23 points from last October. Some 43 percent of Brits see her as decisive, with 40 percent regarding her as competent. But with just one in five Britons believing her Conservative Party is ready to govern again — and the party now facing a more popular adversary in No. 10 Downing Street in Andy Burnham — strategists are eyeing an autumn blitz putting Badenoch to the fore. Advertisement Advertisement “Kemi is popular. We are trying to promote the rest of the shadow Cabinet to make sure that popularity rubs off on the rest of the party,” said one Badenoch staffer, granted anonymity because they were not authorized to speak on the record. So far, it hasn’t worked. “Badenoch’s success has still failed to translate into any meaningful movement in the polls for her party,” said Scarlett Maguire, founder of independent polling firm Merlin Strategy. “The Conservatives’ mediocre polling numbers, still worse than when they lost the 2024 election, shows the extent to which they have lost trust in their brand.” New look conference The party’s first big set piece moment this autumn will come when the Conservative Party meets for its annual conference in Birmingham at the beginning of October. Badenoch’s performance at last year’s gathering marked the beginning of her transformation as party leader, and her team is hoping to repeat the trick by making this year’s conference more Badenoch-focused. There will be less policy this year, according to one shadow minister familiar with the plans and also granted anonymity to speak freely. Advertisement Advertisement “Last year was a bit scattergun. There was a bit too much policy, trying to prove we had something to say. This will be about putting Kemi forward as an alternative to Andy Burnham,” this person said. “People see Burnham as someone who blows with the wind a bit, so [we] want to push forward the theme that Kemi is someone who doesn’t change her mind, is guided by a strong set of principles and isn’t going to change just to be popular,” the same shadow minister added. Viral economics Hot on the heels of party conference season will be the Burnham administration’s first budget, currently penciled in for Oct. 28. Strategists hope it will give them a chance to promote the party’s “sound” economic vision. Badenoch’s response to last year’s budget went “viral” — and is seen as a key moment when the public started to see the Tory leader differently. It is Badenoch and not Shadow Chancellor Mel Stride who is “calling the shots” on economic strategy, according to another member of the shadow Cabinet. Advertisement Advertisement “The economic direction of the party has to come from her, not from Mel,” they said. Badenoch discussed how to shape a right-wing economic vision — in particular the challenge of keeping wealthy people from leaving the country — with Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni on Monday, according to the Times. Though shadow ministers and advisors agree long-serving Conservatives like Stride will help give Badenoch credibility within the business community. “We need to get to a point where we’ve got a real economic narrative. That’s what Kemi’s team are hoping will be the transformative thing,” said the same shadow Cabinet minister quoted above. Reform, interrupted The mood in Tory ranks has also been bolstered by a difficult few months for Reform’s Farage, who has faced questions over whether he properly declared donations. MPs and strategists were delighted Farage spent his summer tied up in the Clacton by-election triggered by his own resignation in July, leaving Badenoch clear to be the main critic of the newly crowned Burnham. Advertisement Advertisement Tory MPs gleefully claim those who defected from their party to Reform are starting to look differently at the Reform UK leader. “The change in the Conservatives has been substantial, but there has also been a big change in Reform as well,” the shadow Cabinet member quoted above said, pointing to reported splits in Reform over how to approach Farage and and policy areas such as welfare spending. Badenoch’s sharp remark that a pact with Reform would be “monstrous” points firmly to the Tory leader wanting to stand her ground against the threat from the right.

https://www.techtimes.com/articles/32457.text: Apple sent its largest documented single wave of mercenary spyware threat notifications on Thursday, alerting an unspecified number of iPhone users across 110 countries that they may have been individually targeted by government-grade surveillance tools — and for the first time in five years of the program, the warning arrived directly on their Lock Screen. The delivery change matters not only to the individuals who received it: according to Citizen Lab researcher John Scott-Railton, it is the mechanism by which Apple's alert ecosystem turns private warnings into public investigations, catching spyware abusers in ways no other accountability infrastructure can.Five Years of Missed WarningsSince Apple launched its threat notification program in late 2021, warnings have traveled through email — sent from threat-notifications@email.apple.com — plus iMessage and a banner that appears after a user logs into their Apple Account at account.apple.com. All three channels share the same core failure mode: at-risk individuals routinely miss the alerts, filter them as spam, or dismiss them as phishing attempts.That failure is not hypothetical. Mercenary spyware is designed to be invisible; its targets are selected precisely because of who they are and what they know. A journalist covering a government that has purchased Pegasus — NSO Group's flagship iPhone spyware, and the most documented example in this category — may receive an email warning they mistake for the phishing attempts that governments routinely send alongside the attacks. A missed email notification is a missed opportunity to enable the one defense that has never been defeated.In a revised support article published the same day as Thursday's notification wave, Apple confirmed that the warning will now appear as a push alert directly on the iPhone Lock Screen, reading: "Apple detected a mercenary spyware attack targeted at your iPhone. There are actions you can take now to help protect your data and device." A permanent row in the Settings app accompanies the Lock Screen banner — unlike an email, it cannot be cleared without the user absorbing the message. Apple told TechCrunch it has updated the notification user experience to make it easier for recipients to access important information on what to do next.Why Better Alert Delivery Means More Investigations Get StartedThe delivery upgrade is not merely a usability improvement — it is infrastructure for accountability.Scott-Railton, a senior researcher at the University of Toronto's Citizen Lab, was the first to publicly highlight Thursday's notification wave. He told TechCrunch that Apple's push alert system functions as the starting point for investigations that go far beyond any individual target."Notifications create a critical signal that a community is being targeted," Scott-Railton said. "People get an alert, and then some of them reach out and seek help. Often this kicks off an investigation that reveals many, many more cases."He named the ongoing political scandal in Poland as the clearest demonstration of this chain. Under the former Law and Justice government, Pegasus spyware was used against opposition politicians, campaign managers, and civil society figures — including Polish Senator Krzysztof Brejza, who was reportedly targeted dozens of times in 2019 while running the opposition's campaign operation. In December 2024, Polish authorities arrested former spy chief Piotr Pogonowski to compel his testimony before parliament."Without Apple's notifications, that entire massive scandal about spyware abuse in the Polish election wouldn't have been uncovered," Scott-Railton said. An alert that reaches someone who then reaches out to a forensics organization does not just protect one person — it maps a targeting campaign that may have dozens or hundreds of undisclosed victims.What Mercenary Spyware Is and Who Gets TargetedApple's threat notification support page defines these attacks as individually targeted, using tools of exceptional cost and complexity historically associated with state actors, including private companies developing mercenary spyware on their behalf — with Pegasus from NSO Group cited as a prominent example. The targets are typically journalists, activists, politicians, and diplomats, and the cost of deploying these tools means operators are highly selective.Spyware such as Pegasus arrives via "zero-click" attacks — exploits that require no interaction from the target, often delivered through iMessage or WhatsApp by taking advantage of unpatched software vulnerabilities in the way those applications process incoming media. Once installed, the operator can access everything the target's phone sees and hears, including communications sent over end-to-end encrypted applications like Signal and WhatsApp.Apple does not identify the specific spyware behind individual alerts and cannot share what triggers notifications, as disclosing detection methods would help spyware makers adapt their behavior to evade future identification.The commercial spyware industry has expanded well beyond NSO Group. Paragon Solutions' Graphite spyware was documented by Citizen Lab in a March 2025 investigation targeting civil society members in Italy, including journalists and humanitarian workers. Intellexa's Predator has been linked to targeting in the United States and multiple EU member states.NSO Group itself is the subject of active US litigation. A federal court found NSO liable for violating anti-hacking laws in the WhatsApp case, and a jury awarded approximately $167 million in damages in May 2025; a permanent injunction took effect January 28, 2026. Meta filed a contempt motion in June 2026 alleging NSO ran new spyware campaigns against WhatsApp users within days of that injunction taking legal effect.The Target Profile Is Wider Than Most People KnowAdam Boynton, senior enterprise strategy manager at device-management firm Jamf, said the threat profile has expanded beyond the groups most commonly discussed in public reporting. "The economics of mercenary spyware mean the target list increasingly includes executives, negotiators, and anyone holding privileged access," he said. "If one of these notifications lands on a work device, it should be treated as a security incident from the first minute."Boynton noted that these tools "rely on zero-day exploits precisely because the iPhone's defenses leave attackers no cheaper way in" — meaning the device's security architecture is working, but the cost of attacking it is simply absorbed by well-resourced operators rather than serving as a deterrent.Jamf's Mobile Forensics product for enterprise is designed specifically to detect Pegasus, zero-click exploits, and related advanced threats on iOS and Android, and the firm's marketing explicitly lists "traveling executives" and "government officials" alongside journalists and politicians as the population in scope.Lockdown Mode: Apple's Strongest Defense Has a Perfect RecordThe Lock Screen push notification opens directly to a set of recommended actions, the most significant of which is enabling Lockdown Mode — an opt-in security configuration introduced with iOS 16 in 2022 that dramatically shrinks the attack surface available to spyware developers.Apple has confirmed it has yet to see a case where a device running Lockdown Mode was successfully compromised by mercenary spyware. Donncha Ó Cearbhaill, head of Amnesty International's Security Lab, has independently backed that claim, saying that no Lockdown Mode-enabled device has appeared in the organization's forensic analysis as having been compromised by this class of attack.Lockdown Mode achieves this by intentionally limiting iPhone functionality across several surfaces that spyware developers commonly exploit: it disables link previews in Messages, blocks wired connections from unrecognized accessories, restricts certain web browsing technologies, and removes invitation-based features for Apple services including FaceTime and AirDrop. The restriction set is designed not to block specific known exploits — which change constantly — but to eliminate the attack surface those exploits operate against. An exploit that depends on iMessage media parsing has nothing to execute against if link previews are disabled.What Recipients Should Do NowApple's revised threat notification support page and the Lock Screen alert itself direct users to a consistent set of steps.Update immediately. Install the latest available iOS to ensure the device has the most current security patches. Turn on automatic updates if they are not already active.Enable Lockdown Mode. Available in Settings > Privacy & Security. It is Apple's highest-security configuration and has no documented case of being defeated by mercenary spyware. Users do not need to receive a threat notification to enable it — anyone who believes they may be at heightened risk can turn it on at any time.Contact Access Now's Digital Security Helpline. The helpline is free, operates around the clock, and is named by Apple in the notification itself. The Access Now Digital Security Helpline has no information about why Apple flagged a specific device, but can provide tailored advice and conduct a forensic analysis that may uncover evidence of compromise — or confirm the device is clean.Secure the account from a separate, trusted device. This means changing the Apple Account password, reviewing every device signed in to the account, confirming the trusted phone numbers associated with two-factor authentication, and checking Settings > General > VPN & Device Management for configuration profiles that were not personally installed.Alert contacts. If a device was compromised, the exposure includes all conversations on that device — meaning sources, colleagues, and family members who never received an alert may also have had their messages read by an operator.Apple also warns that a legitimate threat notification will never ask users to click a link, open a file, install an app or profile, or provide their Apple Account password. To verify that a notification is genuine, sign in at account.apple.com — if Apple sent a warning, it will appear prominently at the top of the page after sign-in.The Scale of the ProgramApple has sent threat notifications multiple times yearly since 2021 and has now alerted users in more than 150 countries in total. Thursday's wave covering 110 countries is the largest documented single-country-count wave in the program's history — the previous comparable wave covered 100 countries approximately a year ago.Apple characterizes these as high-confidence alerts that a user has been singled out by a mercenary spyware attack and stresses that recipients should take the warning seriously. At the same time, the vast majority of iPhone users will never be targeted by attacks that are by design extremely selective — the expense and operational complexity of deploying government-grade surveillance tools means operators are not running mass campaigns.For the small and growing group that does receive an alert, Thursday's changes mean the warning is now harder to miss, harder to mistake for spam, and — through the embedded guidance to Access Now and Lockdown Mode — more actionable from the moment it appears. Whether that translates into more at-risk individuals actually enabling Lockdown Mode or contacting forensics experts in time remains the open question that researchers like Scott-Railton are watching. But the answer now starts on the Lock Screen, not in a spam filter.Frequently Asked QuestionsIs an Apple threat notification real, or could it be a phishing attempt?A legitimate Apple threat notification appears directly on your iPhone Lock Screen and in your Settings app — it does not arrive only by email and does not ask you to click a link, download a file, or enter your Apple Account password. To verify any notification you receive, sign in at account.apple.com from a browser: if Apple sent a warning, it will appear prominently at the top of the page after you log in. Phishing attempts that mimic these alerts have been documented; the verification step through account.apple.com is the definitive check against fakes.Why does changing how the alert is delivered matter for investigations beyond the individual recipient?Every person who receives an Apple threat notification and then contacts a forensics organization like Access Now or Citizen Lab provides the starting point for an investigation that typically identifies many more targets than just that one device. John Scott-Railton of Citizen Lab pointed to Poland's ongoing spyware abuse investigation — which has implicated the former government in targeting up to 600 people — as a direct product of Apple's notification ecosystem. If recipients miss or dismiss the alert, that investigation never starts. Getting the warning onto the Lock Screen, where it cannot be filtered or quietly deleted, is functionally important to the accountability chain, not only to the individual's protection.What is Lockdown Mode and does it actually stop Pegasus-class spyware?Lockdown Mode is an opt-in security configuration available on iPhone, iPad, and Mac that reduces the attack surface available to spyware developers by disabling iMessage link previews, blocking wired connections from unrecognized accessories, and restricting several other features commonly exploited in zero-click attacks. Apple has confirmed that no device running Lockdown Mode has been successfully compromised by mercenary spyware since the feature launched in 2022. Amnesty International's Security Lab has independently corroborated this finding. Lockdown Mode intentionally restricts some everyday features; users should expect changes in how certain apps behave. It can be enabled in Settings > Privacy & Security and does not require a device wipe or special configuration. The full record and technical details are covered in Apple's Lockdown Mode track record published by TechTimes in March 2026.I'm an executive or work in a sensitive role — should I be concerned even without a threat notification?Yes. Security professionals at Jamf, which makes forensics tools used to detect Pegasus and related spyware on enterprise devices, say the economics of mercenary spyware mean the target list has expanded beyond journalists, activists, and politicians to include corporate executives, senior negotiators, and anyone who holds privileged access to sensitive communications or systems. If your role gives you access to material that a government or a well-resourced adversary would find valuable, you are within the threat model for these tools. Enabling Lockdown Mode is the strongest preventive step available; contacting your organization's security team and establishing a mobile device monitoring protocol — such as periodic forensic analysis — are the next steps for high-risk professional contexts. Jamf's enterprise forensics platform provides detection capabilities for exactly this threat category.

Maverick News Alleged Big Five cartel boss Jothan Msibi was involved in retrieving stolen stock for the controversial tobacco company Carnilinx and was part of a plot to get spyware technology from a Czech company into Eswatini, the Madlanga Commission has heard. By Caryn Dolley 18 Aug 2026 Illustrative image: Jotan Mbisi (Photo: Taxi Media / Facebook) | Tobacco (Photo: iStock) Dive Deeper Speed Read Summary Listen Dive Deeper Controversial tobacco company Carnilinx used alleged Big Five cartel boss Jothan (also spelled Jotham) Msibi to retrieve stolen stock, according to messages screened at the Madlanga Commission on Tuesday, 18 August. Msibi, a taxi industry heavyweight who died in 2024, was also linked during the proceedings to marijuana cultivation, a plot to source and sell spying devices known as grabbers, and questionable dealings around tenders. The connection extending from Msibi to Carnilinx, meanwhile, unravels in different directions; one leads to politics and a murky arena. Alleged Big Five cartel leader Jothan (also spelled Jotham) Msibi. (Photo: IG:Joy-Zelda / X) Who was Jothan (also spelled Jotham) Msibi? It has been alleged that before he died in 2024 following a short illness, taxi industry heavyweight Msibi headed a sprawling criminal cartel known as the Big Five. A senior policeman said that this cartel infiltrated South Africaâs criminal justice sector, politics and private security. Among those at Msibiâs funeral was a former police minister, Bheki Cele. During previous Madlanga Commission proceedings , it emerged that Carnilinx director Adriano Mazzotti (who has been open about making donations to the EFF and ANC ) admitted in 2014 to extensive customs, excise and tax non-compliance. Another Carnilinx thread leads to embattled senior Crime Intelligence officer Feroz Khan. Carnilinx and Khan Khan was wounded in a shooting at the end of June, shortly before he was meant to testify at the Madlanga Commission, where several accusations have been levelled against him â one of which is that he is connected to senior Carnilinx executive Mohammadh Sayed. Crime Intelligence officer Major General Feroz Khan. (Photo: OJ Koloti / Gallo Images) Text messages screened during Tuesdayâs proceedings added Msibiâs name to those tied to Carnilinx. Msibi is linked to an array of figures who have already featured at the Madlanga Commission, which is examining whether the Big Five cartel compromised South African state institutions, politics and the private sector. Read more Feroz Khan â Centrifugal force in SAPS tender dealings with tobacco bosses, inquiry hears July 3, 2026 Some of the messages screened on Tuesday were between Carnilinx director Kyle Phillips and Msibi. âPappa Joe to the rescueâ Evidence leader Matthew Chaskalson, who read out the communication exchange, explained: âWhat we see in these chats [â¦ is that] when Carnilinx gets robbed, they call up Mr Msibi to sort it all out and find out who has robbed them and get their stock back.â One of the messages, dated February 2021, was from Phillips to Msibi, whom he referred to as âPappa Joeâ. It said: âHey Pappa Joe ! Thanks for sorting out â¦ just tell us where to collectâ¦ but please ask if they can recover the fire-arms [sic] as well.â Chaskalson said Phillips was messaging about a theft of stock and firearms. Jothan (also spelled Jotham) Msibiâs alleged connections Carnilinx director Kyle Phillips. Steve Motsumi, who some police officers seemed afraid of. Motsumiâs name has been mentioned alongside Big Five allegations, but he has not been formally identified as part of the cartel. Vusimuzi âCatâ Matlala, accused of various crimes and colluding with police officers, is also alleged to be a Big Five cartel member. Matlala has confirmed he knew Msibi. ANC-linked businessman Suliman Carrim was named by Matlala as knowing Motsumi and visiting Msibiâs farm. Katiso âKTâ Molefe , who is accused of orchestrating several contract killings. Someone identified as âAliâ, possibly the thief or someone who ended up with the stolen stock, had repeatedly messaged Phillips in an apparent panic, saying he wanted to return the stock and talk to Phillips, who appeared to ignore him after an initial greeting. Madlanga Commission evidence leader Matthew Chaskalson says investigators have identified a connection between tobacco company Carnilinx, one of its directors, Kyle Phillips and late taxi boss Mswazi Msibi. The evidence is expected to shed light on the relationship between theâ¦ pic.twitter.com/mxFD8mzFTr — eNCA (@eNCA) August 18, 2026 Another message from Phillips to Msibi mentioned an individual â possibly Ali â who had been contacting his âguysâ and who he told to deal with Msibi. Msibi responded, âHi.Kyle.he spoke to me yesterday at night.he told me the cigar is on u street next to u factory.but he promise to come am also waiting but itâsok as long as he brings back the staff [sic].â Phillips, according to the messages screened on Tuesday, responded to Msibi a few days later, saying: âAfternoon Pappa Joe !!!! All stock is returned.. thank you so so much ! Everything is sorted.â Tender rigging suspicions and Ze Nxumalo Focus on Tuesday also turned to Msibiâs contact with businessman Ze Nxumalo , whose name previously surfaced during Madlanga Commission proceedings. Chaskalson said, âMr Msibi appears to have used Mr Nxumalo to rig a tender for him at Ekurhuluni.â A message apparently from Nxumalo to Msibi, dated 13 June 2023, referred to a bid invitation, asking: âIs it spoken for?â The Madlanga Commission had asked Nxumalo for the âfull detailsâ of the person to whom he wrote that message. MADLANGA COMMISSION | Adv Chaskalson says the evidence suggests Ze Nxumalo routinely interacted with individuals allegedly involved in tender rigging, raising questions about the nature and frequency of those engagements. pic.twitter.com/GVbsaWi7SW — SABC News (@SABCNews) August 18, 2026 Nxumalo responded in a typed statement that Chaskalson described as ârather evasiveâ. Nxumalo said, âI have no recollection of the circumstances in which it came to be sent, and I am accordingly unable to identify the person to whom the words were addressed, or from whom I may have received them.â Nxumalo also disputed that he was the author of the message, saying: âIt is not my manner of typing.â Dealing in grabbers Earlier during Tuesdayâs proceedings, Chaskalson detailed how Msibi had been involved in dealing in international mobile subscriber identity catchers (IMSI-catchers), better known as grabbers . Several others were allegedly involved in the grabber matters alongside Msibi. These include Katiso Molefe, who faces a murder charge; Steve Motsumi , a businessman previously mentioned at the Madlanga Commission as someone police officers are afraid to name; and Gauteng Sergeant Fannie Nkosi, who is facing unrelated charges . Messages between Nkosi and someone saved under the name Shaun Jacobs suggested a questionable project that developed in 2023. What is a grabber? Madlanga Commission evidence leader Matthew Chaskalson explained that grabbers âenable you to eavesdrop on cellphones and extract information from cellphonesâ. Grabbers, he added, mimicked a legitimate cellphone tower and âtrickedâ nearby cellphones to connect to it instead of the legitimate tower. This project was aimed at getting grabbers (or related technology) from a Czech company, Invasys, and channelling the acquisitions to Eswatini. Chaskalson said Nkosi had indicated to the Czech government that Invasys would give a grabber demonstration to South African police, but the actual plan, unbeknownst to the Czech authorities, was to sell grabber technology to Eswatini. (Messages suggested that Msibi, as part of this plan, met with Eswatiniâs king.) Chaskalson said that Nkosiâs signing of documents on behalf of, and purporting to represent, the South African Police Service in deals with international suppliers, suggested âan out and out fraudâ. The grabber plan linked to Eswatini did not pan out. âWorrying state of affairsâ Chaskalson said Msibi, Motsumi and Molefe had, meanwhile, âexplored other options. These three men are dealing with foreign companies to get access to grabber technology purporting to represent a state.â Katiso "KT" Molefe appears in a Johannesburg court on 5 February. (Photo: Lubabalo Lesolle / Gallo Images) The alternate grabber plan had involved Msibi and Motsumi travelling to places including Paris and Zurich. Chaskalson described the situation as âa very worrying state of affairsâ. He emphasised that grabber technology âshould only go into the hands of intelligence agencies who are then constrained to use it under fairly strict legislative controlsâ. Instead, he noted, âPrivate parties passing themselves off as representatives of stateâ had gained access to the technology and were attempting to trade in it. DM What next? National Coloured Congress leader Fadiel Adams is expected to testify before the Madlanga Commission on Wednesday, 19 August, with a probable focus on his role in apparently sparking controversial investigations against Crime Intelligence officers. The commission aims to wrap up its hearings by early October, after which it will complete a report on the hearings and present it to President Cyril Ramaphosa. https://www.rferl.org/a/moscow-is-making.text: Accessibility links Skip to main content Skip to main Navigation Skip to Search Print Options: Images Multimedia Embedded Content Comments Russia For Russians Abroad, Renouncing Their Citizenship Is Getting Harder -- And More Expensive By Artyom Filatov August 23, 2026 09:29 CET Listen 7 min This audio is automated Learn more For Russians Abroad, Renouncing Their Citizenship Is Getting Harder -- And More Expensive Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Prefer us on Google Russian passport. Vlada Kharebova has been trying to renounce her Russian citizenship since 2022, without success so far. Kharebova lives in Latvia and is seeking citizenship for herself and her two children there. But the Baltic nation generally does not allow dual citizenship in such cases: The law indicates dual Latvian-Russian citizenship is not permitted. She has run into problems with the Russian consulate in Riga, which she said provides a list of required documents but little guidance on how to obtain them. "When you call or write to the consulate, they say: 'We don't deal with this. Sorry, we can't help,'" Kharebova told Current Time. Russia has also increased the fees for this process, now making it "a significantly high amount" for her to pay on her salary as a teacher. Her daughter encountered an obstacle when the consulate refused to accept her application because she had not brought a copy of her college diploma from Russia. Kharebova said the requirement was not listed in the available instructions. For Russians who live abroad who want to give up their Russian citizenship, be it for legal, bureaucratic, or moral reasons or a combination of factors, the process can take years. And it just got considerably more expensive, for those inside and outside Russia. Vlada Kharebova speaks to Current Time correspondent Artyom Filatov. (Screengrab) A new law that took effect on July 22 raised the state duty for renouncing citizenship from 4,200 rubles ($50) to 50,000 rubles ($592), while a separate government resolution raised the consular fee for applications submitted abroad from $130 to $1,200. The increase piles another problem onto a process that applicants abroad say can be difficult to navigate. Finnish resident Veronika Mikkonen said some documents required for the procedure are valid for only three months. That can create a race against time, particularly when applicants struggle to secure an appointment at a Russian diplomatic mission -- something that can also take months. Mikkonen eventually succeeded in renouncing her citizenship but said preparing the documents cost her nearly 1,000 euros ($1,160) even though the consular fee at the time was 130 euros ($152). Mikkonen suggested her decision was motivated by the Kremlin's repression at home and the full-scale invasion of Ukraine, launched by President Vladimir Putin in February 2022. "I just didn't want to carry in my pocket the passport of a dictatorial country and a country that started a war," she told Current Time. Moscow Stopped Publishing Stats The Russian Foreign Ministry has not published nationwide figures on citizenship renunciations since 2023. Its publicly reported figures show 4,356 people renounced Russian citizenship in 2019, 3,877 in 2020, 4,055 in 2021, and 4,306 in 2022, the first year of the full-scale war. The ministry said the 2022 figure did not represent a significant change in the trend. In the first nine months of 2023, about 4,400 people renounced their citizenship, according to the head of the Foreign Ministry's Consular Department. Hundreds of thousands of Russians fled abroad after Putin announced a large-scale military mobilization in September 2022. SEE ALSO: Anti-War Russians Abroad Fear Kremlin Covertly Pressuring Hosts To Send Them Back The absence of updated state statistics makes it difficult to determine whether the number of people seeking to give up their Russian citizenship has increased as the invasion continues with little sign of an end in sight. But data from individual countries suggests that demand is significant. Estonia registered 107 people having renounced Russian citizenship in 2024. By August 25, 2025, the figure for that year had already reached 126, according to the country's Interior Ministry. Estonia also reported persistent delays: The Russian Embassy in Tallinn stopped accepting new renunciation applications from late 2023 until February 2024 following the entry into force of a new Russian citizenship law. After processing resumed, long lines remained because Russia had closed its consulates in the cities of Tartu and Narva and reduced staffing at the embassy in Tallinn. Russian consulates in several other cities in Europe and elsewhere have been closed amid high tensions between Moscow and the West over the invasion of Ukraine and other issues. Foreigners seeking Estonian citizenship through naturalization generally have to give up their existing citizenship. The delays at the Russian Embassy have therefore created a problem for people who need proof they are no longer Russian citizens before they can complete the naturalization process. 'I Have Nothing To Do With Russia' Russian law also places conditions on renunciation. Applicants must have another citizenship or a guarantee of its receipt, and renunciation can be denied if the applicant has outstanding taxes, fees, and fines or certain unresolved legal obligations. For some applicants, the question is not whether they want to leave Russia but whether they can afford, navigate, and complete the process. Madrid resident Aleksandr Smirnov, who obtained Spanish citizenship, told Current Time that he has tried without success to renounce his Russian citizenship. Aleksandr Smirnov After the fee increase, he said, he was unsure whether it would be worth continuing the process. "I haven't been to Russia for 10 years, I have nothing to do with Russia, I have no property or bank accounts there. I don't need this citizenship," he told Current Time. "I would like to renounce it so that I have just one citizenship, of the country where I live. That's logical. But my feeling is that their goal is to put obstacles in the way." Human rights activist Lev Ponomaryov agrees, saying he believes the Russian authorities are interested in making renunciation a procedure that is difficult to access. "They don't want there to be a large flow of people renouncing [their citizenship], so that it becomes a kind of information bomb that more and more people are giving up Russian citizenship," he said. Sells 7.6 MWp of PV Operational Assets in Slovakia EQS-News: Photon Energy NV / Key word(s): Disposal Photon Energy N.V. Sells 7.6 MWp of PV Operational Assets in Slovakia 26.09.2026 / 00:01 CET/CEST The issuer is solely responsible for the content of this announcement. Company: Photon Energy N.V. Date: 2026-09-25 Title: Photon Energy N.V. Sells 7.6 MWp of PV Operational Assets in Slovakia Detailed data: The management board of Photon Energy N.V. informs that it has entered into an agreement for the sale of eight photovoltaic power plants in Slovakia with a total installed capacity of 7.581 MWp (the "Portfolio"). The Portfolio comprises eight wholly owned special purpose vehicles (SPVs) operating photovoltaic power plants in Slovakia namely: EcoPlan 2 and 3 located in Mokra Luka (963 kWp each), Fotonika (999 kWp), Sun4ZVB and SUN4ZVC located in Babina (999 kWp each), SK SPV 2 and 3 located in Jovice (979 kWp each), and ATS Energy located in Blatná (700 kWp). The whole Portfolio was sold to four private individuals who are strategic investors in PV assets in Slovakia. The Portfolio transaction was structured as a sale of shares in the SPV companies at an enterprise valuation of EUR 5.6 million, payable upon completion of the transaction. The Portfolio generated revenues of approximately EUR 2.1 million and EBITDA of approximately EUR 1.65 million in 2025. As of 30 June 2026, the Portfolio had outstanding project financing of approximately EUR 4.1 million, which remains with the sold SPV companies and thus the Group's financial debt is reduced by this amount. The transaction forms a part of the Group's ongoing efforts to optimize its asset portfolio, reduce financial debt, strengthen its liquidity position and facilitate the envisaged restructuring process. According to the Company's assessment, the assets have a limited remaining feed-in tariff support period until 2030 or 2031 and require additional investment in connection with material capital expenditure obligations before year-end 2026. These investment commitments arise from the extension of the feed-in-tariff period from 15 to 20 years introduced in 2021 and expose the Group to certain regulatory uncertainties. A detailed analysis of the long-term repowering options after the end of the feed-in-tariff scheme for the Slovak portfolio, conducted in 2023, highlighted the unavailability of additional grid capacity and severe limitations on the extension of land usage rights, severely limiting value upside from repowering. In light of these considerations, and the Group's objective to limit further capital-intensive investments, the Company considers the divestment of the Portfolio an appropriate strategic step. The Group continues owning 50% stakes in three PV power plants in Slovakia (Myjava, Polianka and Brestovec) with a total installed capacity of 2.85 MWp. Land ownership and the plants' proximity to potential future energy users provide better long-term optionality than the power plants sold in the transaction. The project financing on these three joint venture power plants have been fully repaid in 2025 and thus they provide ongoing unencumbered free cash flow to the Group. Upon completion of the transaction, the Group expects to reduce consolidated financial debt by approximately EUR 4.1 million as a result of deconsolidation, reduce required capital expenditures and related regulatory risks, secure funding to facilitate the envisaged restructuring process in the interest of the joint creditors and provide additional resources for the Group's immediate financing and working capital requirements, which are expected to benefit all stakeholders. 26.09.2026 CET/CEST Dissemination of a Corporate News, transmitted by EQS News - a service of EQS Group . Photograph: Susannah Ireland/The Guardian UK unemployment and employment statistics Surprise drop in UK unemployment to 4.7% as John Healey’s first budget looms Latest ONS data presents mixed picture amid slump in job vacancies and analysts warning labour market is ‘running on idle’ Business live – news updates Healey to reject calls to raise CGT in budget Phillip Inman Senior economics writer and Graeme Wearden Tue 20 Oct 2026 04.39 EDT First published on Tue 20 Oct 2026 02.29 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Unemployment in the UK has fallen unexpectedly in the final snapshot of the jobs market before John Healey’s first budget next week. The jobless rate fell to 4.7% in the three months to August, from 4.9% according to the Office for National Statistics . City economists had forecast a rise to 5%. In a further boost to the chancellor, the figures also showed that the number of payrolled employees rose by 13,000 between August and September, to 30.3m. However, a slump in the number of job vacancies illustrated what some economists said was an economy moving sideways. After hitting a peak of 1.3m in the period after the pandemic, vacancies fell by 21,000 to 691,000 in the three months to September, the lowest since 2021 during the Covid pandemic. Neet rates higher in England’s smaller cities and towns than in biggest cities Read more Ben Harrison, director of the Work Foundation thinktank at Lancaster University, said the fall in unemployment “should not make the government complacent ahead of next week’s budget”. He said: “The UK is still amidst a jobs drought with vacancies at their lowest for over 12 years outside of the pandemic.” Data on wage growth was mixed. Stripping out bonuses, average pay growth rose to 3.7% from 3.6%.Hoever, when bonuses are included the rate fell to 3.7% from 3.9%, indicating that few bonuses were paid to workers. Wage growth in the UK remains above inflation, which was 3.1% in August and is expected to rise to 3.4% when figures for September are published on Wednesday. The Bank of England is widely expected to raise interest rates in response to higher prices at next month’s meeting of the monetary policy committee. The pound rose against the dollar after the labour market figures were released, by about half a cent to $1.3352. The ONS estimated there were 715,000 unemployed young people aged 16 to 24, down by 28,000 on the quarter. Harrison said ministers should be more focused on the number of jobless young people remaining at 54,000 higher than 12 months ago. Suren Thiru, chief economistInstitute of Chartered Accountants in England and Wales, described the labour market as “running on idle” with employers limiting recruitment and pay awards “in response to surging cost pressures and pre-budget policy uncertainty”. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Business Today Get set for the working day – we'll point you to all the business news and analysis you need every morning after newsletter promotion He said: “The continued fall in vacancies is a flashing red warning light for the labour market, suggesting that a damaging side-effect of this year’s AI-fuelled economic growth has been weaker hiring demand, compounded by elevated employment costs.” Average pay growth remains above the 3.1% headline rate of inflation, which is of concern to Bank of England interest rate setters, who fear higher-than-expected inflation will translate into higher pay awards, fuelling future price rises recorded by the consumer prices index (CPI). Financial markets expect interest rates to rise to between 4.75% and 5% by the middle of next year, although the consultancy Capital Economics said recent improvements in the labour market were modest and the central bank would probably cap interest rates at 4.25%. The secretary of state for work and pensions, Pat McFadden, said: “Today’s figures show the resilience of our labour market with unemployment falling and the UK’s employment rate now the third highest in the G7, despite a backdrop of global uncertainty.” But he conceded that many young people needed support to enter the labour market. “That’s why we are working with industry, to bring young people back into the labour market and prevent them from drifting into the welfare system.” Explore more on these topics UK unemployment and employment statistics Economics Inflation Pay Unemployment and employment statistics Unemployment Family finances news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed Business Economics Diversity & equality in business Small business Retail
